newsitem.title: GERMANY: German prosecutors charge five in arson probe.
newsitem.headline: German prosecutors charge five in arson probe.

text.p: Prosecutors said on Wednesday they had charged four residents of an east German village and another from a town nearby in connection with an arson attack on a local refugees' hostel.

News reports and some investigators have suggested that a widespread conspiracy in the village of Dolgenbrodt, south of Berlin, lay behind the 1992 firebomb attack the day before 86 asylum seekers were due to move into the new hostel.
A young right-winger, Silvio Jakowski, has already been convicted for the firebombing.

But prosecutors said they now believed Jakowski had merely acted as lookout and that one of the five new suspects, identified only as Renato P. from the nearby town of Koenigs Wusterhausen, actually carried out the attack.
Prosecutor Wolfgang Lehmann said the likely reason for the attack was a widespread belief in the village that the hostel's presence would hit property prices in the area.

Investigators believe one of those charged, a local florist, was the mastermind behind the attack. The man has already confessed to paying young extremists to firebomb the building but denies anyone else in the village was involved.
Four of the five are charged with arson and weapons offences while a fifth is charged with assisting the arson. Four are also charged with giving false testimony at Jakowski's trial.
